Overall, predictive modeling for dysphagia in older adults remains in an early stage, limited by methodological flaws and insufficient external validation. Future research should follow PROBAST standards and conduct large, multicenter validations to improve model reliability and clinical utility.

records.title: Artificial intelligence advances in cystoscopy and imaging for bladder cancer: a narrative review.

content.title: Artificial intelligence advances in cystoscopy and imaging for bladder cancer: a narrative review.
content.abstract: Bladder cancer (BCa) diagnosis relies heavily on cystoscopy and imaging. Both have limited sensitivity and accuracy, particularly for muscle-invasive disease. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising tool for improving detection, grading, and staging by extracting imaging features that exceed human perception. We conducted a narrative review of peer-reviewed, English-language studies published between 2015 and 2025. We identified 75 articles and synthesized data from 35 key studies retrieved via PubMed, Google Scholar, Scopus, and Embase. Data were synthesized narratively, emphasizing diagnostic performance, clinical relevance, and study limitations. In cystoscopy, AI models achieved high accuracy in tumour detection and grading, including carcinoma in situ, and in some studies reduced missed lesions by >20% compared with expert urologists; CystoNet-T reported an average precision of 91.4%. Performance varied across studies, with inconsistencies driven by methodological factors: endoscopic acquisition conditions (illumination quality; white-light vs. enhanced imaging), variation in ground truth and annotation (histopathology vs. expert-labelled frames), dataset size and class imbalance, model architecture and preprocessing pipelines, and validation strategy (internal splits vs. external testing). Most evidence remains limited by retrospective, single-center datasets, which restrict generalizability. In imaging, AI applications showed modality-dependent performance. CT-based radiomic and deep-learning models demonstrated the most consistent improvements for grading, staging, and recurrence prediction across several studies. MRI and radiogenomic models demonstrated proof-of-concept associations between imaging features and molecular profiles. However, clinical readiness is limited by small cohorts and a lack of prospective validation. Results were also affected by scanner heterogeneity and reader dependence. Evidence for PET/CT remains sparse and preliminary. Many approaches outperformed conventional clinical models, including a vision transformer (ViT)-based MRI model for muscle invasiveness prediction (AUC = 0.872). Methodological heterogeneity restricted generalisability. AI shows potential to reduce diagnostic variability and improve initial treatment planning in BCa. Nonetheless, prospective multicentre trials with standardised methodology are essential before clinical integration. In parallel, regulatory approval of AI as medical software, real-time workflow integration within cystoscopy suites and radiology systems, data governance and patient privacy, and ongoing post-deployment performance monitoring must be addressed to ensure safe and effective clinical use.

records.title: Multimodal AI fusion: integrating MRI with PET/CT, histopathology, and liquid biopsy for bone tumor diagnosis.

content.title: Multimodal AI fusion: integrating MRI with PET/CT, histopathology, and liquid biopsy for bone tumor diagnosis.
content.abstract: The diagnosis of bone tumors, though a low-incidence occurrence, presents a formidable challenge due to the morphological heterogeneity and variable biological behavior of these lesions. No single diagnostic modality whether imaging or biopsy is sufficient to provide the comprehensive information necessary for definitive diagnosis, accurate staging, and effective treatment planning. This report argues that a fragmented, sequential approach to diagnosis is inherently limited and that the future of orthopedic oncology lies in the integration of diverse data streams. Multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) offers a promising supportive approach by creating an AI-enabled integrative decision-support environment where computational systems can synthesize and contextualize information from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), positron emission tomography computed tomography (PET/CT), histopathology, and liquid biopsy. This report details the specific capabilities and limitations of each of these foundational modalities, outlines the technical architectures required for their fusion, and illustrates how an integrated AI system can augment clinical workflows. It also addresses the critical challenges that must be overcome for clinical adoption, including data standardization, algorithmic interpretability, and economic viability, ultimately positioning this approach as an important emerging direction for future precision oncology.

records.title: The impact of SGLT2 inhibitors on renal outcomes in patients with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease: systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: The impact of SGLT2 inhibitors on renal outcomes in patients with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease: systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Objective

To analyze and evaluate the impact of SGLT2 inhibitors on the renal outcomes of patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and chronic kidney disease, and to provide evidence-based basis for clinical rational treatment.

Methods

Relevant literatures on the impact of SGLT2 inhibitors on the renal outcomes of patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and chronic kidney disease published in domestic and foreign databases were retrieved and collected. The time limit was from the establishment of each database to November 2025. After screening, the quality of the research literature was evaluated using the Cochrane library. Literature management was conducted using NoteExpress 3.2, and data collection and extraction were carried out using Excel 2003. Statistical analysis was performed using RevMan 5.4.1 software. Based on the size of the Q test (P value), it was determined whether there was heterogeneity in the studies, and then the fixed or random effect model was used to calculate the combined effect OR value, and a forest plot was drawn. Then, the publication bias was evaluated by drawing a funnel plot.

Results

A total of 10 studies that met the inclusion criteria were finally included. The meta-analysis results showed that compared with the control group, the eGFR and CrCI levels of patients treated with 5 mg dapagliflozin showed a more significant decline, renal-related adverse events (OR = 0.91, 95% CI: 0.84 to 0.99, P = 0.04), and the occurrence of doubling of serum creatinine, end-stage renal disease, and renal death events (OR = 0.68, 95% CI: 0.60 to 0.78, P < 0.00001). However, there was no statistically significant difference in acute kidney injury or failure between the two groups. Sensitivity analysis suggested that the results of this study were stable and reliable.

Conclusion

SGLT2 inhibitors can cause a short-term decline in eGFR and CrCl, and significantly reduce the risk of renal composite endpoint events. This indicates that their early hemodynamic effects are predictable physiological changes.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261294499, identifier CRD420261294499.

records.title: Personalization of Training and Weight Reduction Using Artificial Intelligence: A Scoping Review of Current Evidence and Practical Limitations.
records.publisher: Journal of functional morphology and kinesiology

content.title: Personalization of Training and Weight Reduction Using Artificial Intelligence: A Scoping Review of Current Evidence and Practical Limitations.
content.abstract: Background and Objectives: Artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly emerged as a promising tool for delivering personalized interventions in physical activity, exercise prescription, and weight management. AI technologies may facilitate individualized recommendations, behavioral support, and lifestyle modification through adaptive digital health solutions, although their effectiveness remains to be established across different populations and settings. However, the current evidence remains heterogeneous, and the practical implementation of AI in personalized training and weight management requires further evaluation. This scoping review aimed to summarize the current evidence regarding the application of artificial intelligence for the personalization of training and weight reduction, with particular emphasis on the types of AI technologies used, their reported outcomes, practical applications, and current limitations. Methods: A scoping review was conducted following a structured literature search of studies investigating AI-supported interventions related to physical activity, exercise, dietary behavior, and weight management. Eight studies involving diverse populations, intervention designs, and AI technologies were included. Data were extracted on study characteristics, AI technologies, intervention characteristics, reported outcomes, and research gaps. The literature search was subject to access-based restrictions, including the use of "Free full text" in PubMed and "Open Access" in Web of Science, as well as language restrictions. Results: The included studies investigated a wide range of AI technologies, including conversational chatbots, natural language processing systems, machine learning algorithms, computer vision applications, knowledge-based systems, and large language models. Selected studies reported favorable or modest changes in exercise adherence, physical activity participation, dietary behaviors, user engagement, and weight-related outcomes; however, the magnitude and consistency of these findings varied across studies. Personalized coaching, real-time feedback, and continuous behavioral support were common features of interventions reporting favorable outcomes. However, considerable heterogeneity existed across study designs, participant populations, intervention protocols, AI technologies, and outcome measures, and evidence regarding long-term effectiveness remains limited. The findings should be interpreted in the context of the adopted search strategy, including access-based restrictions and the inability to retrieve eight of 57 reports sought for retrieval, which may have contributed to availability bias. Conclusions: Current evidence suggests that artificial intelligence may have potential as a tool for supporting the personalization of training and weight management interventions, particularly through individualized behavioral support, feedback, and user engagement. However, the available evidence is heterogeneous and does not yet allow firm conclusions regarding the effectiveness or mechanisms of AI-supported interventions. AI should currently be viewed as a complement rather than a replacement for healthcare and exercise professionals. Future large-scale randomized controlled trials with longer follow-up periods and standardized outcome measures are needed to clarify the effectiveness, sustainability, and practical implementation of AI-supported interventions.

records.title: Efficacy of laparoscopic transabdominal preperitoneal (TAPP) and totally extraperitoneal (TEP) repair in the treatment of bilateral inguinal hernia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Efficacy of laparoscopic transabdominal preperitoneal (TAPP) and totally extraperitoneal (TEP) repair in the treatment of bilateral inguinal hernia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background and objective

Inguinal hernia is a common general-surgical disease. Laparoscopic repair is widely used for bilateral cases. The practical trade-offs between laparoscopic transabdominal preperitoneal (TAPP) and totally extraperitoneal (TEP) repair remain debated, and most existing publications focus on unilateral inguinal hernia.

Methods

We searched multiple domestic and international databases for comparative studies of TAPP versus TEP for bilateral inguinal hernia. Literature retrieval covered records from database inception to April 6, 2026. Evaluated outcomes included general complications, special complications, recurrence, postoperative pain, operative time, and length of hospital stay. Statistical analyses were performed with RevMan 5.3 and Stata 18.

Results

Nine eligible studies involving 1,319 patients were included (846 patients in the TAPP group and 473 in the TEP group). Pooled data show no significant between-group differences for general complications, special complications, postoperative pain, operative time, and length of hospital stay (all P > 0.05). The overall pooled result indicated a trend toward lower short-term recurrence with TAPP, which was largely driven by retrospective non-randomized cohort data. Although the RCT subgroup yielded a borderline nominally significant result, this signal derived from very limited trial data and does not establish a genuine between-group difference in recurrence risk. Given the maximum follow-up of 12 months across eligible studies, this recurrence-related finding warrants cautious interpretation.

Conclusion

TAPP and TEP deliver comparable short-term safety and efficacy for bilateral inguinal hernia repair. The observed trend of lower short-term recurrence for TAPP relies heavily on observational cohort data and receives no support from RCT evidence. We cannot draw definitive conclusions about recurrence benefits. Further large-sample, long-term high-quality studies are needed.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence for Predicting Amputation and Related Outcomes in Peripheral Artery Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence for Predicting Amputation and Related Outcomes in Peripheral Artery Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Peripheral artery disease (PAD) affects over 236 million individuals globally and carries substantial risks of amputation, major adverse limb events (MALE), and mortality. Existing clinical scoring systems focus on short-term surgical outcomes and lack generalizability. Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a promising tool for PAD outcome prediction.

Objective

To conduct the first quantitative meta-analysis evaluating the discriminative performance, methodological rigor, and certainty of evidence of ML-based prognostic models for adverse limb outcomes in PAD.

Methods

Following PRISMA/PRISMA-S guidelines, PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception through March 15, 2026. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and PROBAST risk-of-bias assessment. Random-effects meta-analysis (DerSimonian-Laird with Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman correction) and hierarchical summary ROC (HSROC) analysis were performed; certainty was rated with GRADE.

Results

Ten studies were included. The pooled AUC for amputation-related outcomes was 0.88 (95% CI, 0.83-0.94; prediction interval, 0.79-0.98) with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 95.4%). HSROC yielded pooled sensitivity 0.855 and specificity 0.836. Registry-based studies showed higher pooled AUC than non-registry studies (0.92 vs 0.80; p = 0.004). All models had high or unclear risk of bias in the analysis domain; none underwent independent external validation. GRADE certainty was very low.

Conclusions

ML models demonstrate high discriminative performance for predicting amputation-related outcomes in PAD, but very low certainty of evidence, absence of external validation, and high risk of bias currently limit clinical implementation. Prospective multicenter validation and adherence to AI reporting guidelines are essential before clinical translation.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence-driven Biomarker Discovery for Precision Psychiatry.
records.publisher: Clinical psychopharmacology and neuroscience : the official scientific journal of the Korean College of Neuropsychopharmacology

content.title: Artificial Intelligence-driven Biomarker Discovery for Precision Psychiatry.
content.abstract: Poor phenotype quality and small cohorts remain major constraints in psychiatric biomarker research, and recent methodological advances increasingly address them. Language models turn clinical text into analysable variables at a scale manual chart review cannot reach. Self-supervised models learn from the unlabelled signals psychiatry already collects. Variant-effect prediction makes molecular interpretation computable, and research agents have generated and experimentally confirmed candidates outside psychiatry. These capabilities act early, on what is measured, what can be learned from it and which candidates are proposed. None of the artificial intelligence capabilities reviewed here yet reaches the stages at which a candidate becomes a clinical test. Producing candidates is becoming cheap while qualifying them is not. This review is organised around that asymmetry rather than by disorder or marker catalogue. It separates the measured characteristic, the prediction model and the intended clinical use, and treats method family as distinct from evidential stage. Across the selected evidence, discrimination is supported more strongly in development data than in independent evaluation, and prospective evidence that model-guided use improves care is scarce. Many reported metrics also address a simpler task than the intended decision: diagnosis instead of differential diagnosis, general prognosis instead of differential treatment benefit. The review proposes a six-stage framework linking intended use, measurement validity, model evaluation, comparative utility and monitored deployment, and places each capability on it, clarifying where methodological progress can accelerate discovery and where conventional clinical validation remains indispensable.

records.title: Artificial intelligence versus manual screening for the detection of diabetic retinopathy: a comparative systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Artificial intelligence versus manual screening for the detection of diabetic retinopathy: a comparative systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Diabetic retinopathy is one of the leading causes of blindness globally, among individuals with diabetes mellitus. Early detection through screening can help in preventing disease progression. In recent advancements artificial Intelligence assisted screening has emerged as an alternative to traditional manual screening methods. This diagnostic test accuracy (DTA) review aims to compare the sensitivity and specificity of AI versus manual screening for detecting diabetic retinopathy, focusing on both dilated and un-dilated eyes.

Methods

A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted for comparison of AI vs. manual screening of diabetic retinopathy using 25 observational (cross sectional, validation and cohort) studies with total images of 613,690 used for screening published between January 2015 and December 2024. Outcomes of the study was sensitivity, and specificity. Risk of bias was assessed using the QUADAS-2 tool for validation studies, the AXIS tool for cross-sectional studies, and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale for cohort studies.

Results

The results of this meta-analysis showed that for un-dilated eyes, AI screening showed pooled sensitivity of 0.90 [95% CI: 0.85-0.94] and pooled specificity of 0.94 [95% CI: 0.91-0.96] while manual screening shows pooled sensitivity of 0.79 [95% CI: 0.60-0.91] and pooled specificity of 0.99 [95% CI: 0.98-0.99]. For dilated eyes the pooled sensitivity of AI screening is 0.95 [95% CI: 0.91-0.97] and pooled specificity is 0.87 [95% CI: 0.79-0.92], while manual screening sensitivity is 0.90 [95% CI: 0.87-0.92] and specificity is 0.99 [95% CI: 0.99-1.00]. These data show comparable sensitivities and specificities of AI and manual screening, with AI performing better in sensitivity.

Conclusion

AI-assisted screening for diabetic retinopathy shows comparable sensitivity and specificity compared to manual screening. These results suggest that AI can be a reliable alternative in clinical settings, with increased early detection rates and reducing the burden on ophthalmologists. Further research is needed to validate these findings.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/home, CRD42024596611.

records.title: Two-decade dialogue between artificial intelligence and osteoporosis: research trajectories and frontier projections under bibliometric and visual analysis.

content.title: Two-decade dialogue between artificial intelligence and osteoporosis: research trajectories and frontier projections under bibliometric and visual analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

This study systematically evaluated the intellectual progress in artificial intelligence (AI)-driven osteoporosis research between 2004 and 2024 by employing scientometric and visualization techniques. Through mapping knowledge domains and identifying emerging trends, it offered actionable recommendations and strategic insights to guide future scholarly endeavors.

Methods

We queried the Web of Science Core Collection for English-language articles and reviews published between January 1, 2004, and November 30, 2024, using search terms including "osteoporosis," "deep learning," "convolutional neural networks," and "artificial intelligence." Bibliometric data were processed via VOSviewer (v1.6.20), CiteSpace (v6.3.R1), Scimago Graphica (v 1.0.46), and the R package Bibliometrix to quantify annual publication trends, assess national/institutional contributions, evaluate journal/author impact metrics, and map keyword co-occurrence and burst dynamics.

Results

The bibliometric analysis identified 408 publications (343 articles, 65 reviews) from 2004 to 2024, with a marked increase in output observed in 2024. China and the United States dominated scholarly productivity and citation impact. Leading institutions included the Technical University of Munich and Seoul National University, while Osteoporosis International emerged as the most influential journal. Prolific authors such as Thomas Baum demonstrated significant academic leadership. Keyword co-occurrence analysis revealed deep learning, artificial intelligence, and diagnosis as core research frontiers, signaling future technological and clinical priorities.

Conclusion

This study represents the first comprehensive bibliometric analysis of research on artificial intelligence in the field of osteoporosis. It not only outlines the field's development trajectory and emerging frontiers but also highlights the research focus on AI technologies, particularly deep learning. Furthermore, it emphasizes critical challenges in clinical translation, such as algorithm optimization, model interpretability, and ethical privacy concerns. By systematically identifying key contributors, collaborative networks, and evolving research fronts, this study provides a foundational roadmap for the field. It offers strategic priorities for researchers to address methodological gaps, serves as a reference for clinicians to understand the evolving technological toolkit, and provides a basis for policymakers to promote interdisciplinary collaboration.

records.title: Artificial intelligence in thyroid eye disease imaging: A systematic review.

content.title: Artificial intelligence in thyroid eye disease imaging: A systematic review.
content.abstract: Thyroid eye disease (TED) is a common, complex orbital disorder characterized by soft-tissue changes visible on imaging. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers promises for improving TED diagnosis and treatment; however, no systematic review has yet characterized the research landscape, key challenges, and future directions. We followed PRISMA guidelines to search multiple databases until January, 2025, for studies applying AI to computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging, and nuclear, facial or retinal imaging in TED patients. Using the APPRAISE-AI tool, we assessed study quality and included 41 studies covering various AI applications. Sample sizes ranged from 33 to 2288 participants, predominantly East Asian. CT and facial imaging were the most common modalities, reported in 16 and 13 articles, respectively. Studies addressed clinical tasks-diagnosis, activity assessment, severity classification, and treatment prediction-and technical tasks-classification, segmentation, and image generation-with classification being the most frequent. Researchers primarily employed deep-learning models, such as residual network (ResNet) and Visual Geometry Group (VGG). Overall, the majority of the studies were of moderate quality. Image-based AI shows strong potential to improve diagnostic accuracy and guide personalized treatment strategies in TED. Future research should prioritize robust study designs, the creation of public datasets, multimodal imaging integration, and interdisciplinary collaboration to accelerate clinical translation.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Peritoneal Dialysis: Applications, Algorithms, and Future Directions.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Peritoneal Dialysis: Applications, Algorithms, and Future Directions.
content.abstract:
Background

Peritoneal dialysis (PD) naturally lends itself to artificial intelligence (AI) due to its generation of dense, longitudinal, and structured data. PD outcomes are strongly influenced by modifiable factors such as dialysate composition, dwell time, and fluid balance, making prediction directly actionable.

Summary

Recent investigations have demonstrated the potential of machine learning and deep learning approaches across multiple domains of PD care. Applications include pre-dialysis patient stratification, prediction of technique failure, monitoring of dialysis adequacy, and assessment of fluid status. AI models have also been developed for forecasting the causative pathogen in peritonitis and prediction of complications, hospitalizations, and mortality, frequently outperforming conventional statistical methods. In parallel, AI-driven chatbots and digital platforms have shown promise in enhancing patient education, engagement, and adherence. While these findings highlight significant potential, most studies to date are single-center, exploratory, and limited in scale, underscoring the need for rigorous external validation and systematic clinical implementation.

Key messages

AI holds considerable promises for improving outcomes in PD by enabling risk identification, individualized therapy, and strengthened patient support. Future directions include integration with electronic health records, remote monitoring, and multi-omics data. Careful validation, ethical safeguards, and equitable deployment will be essential to realize AI's role as a transformative tool in PD care.

records.title: Evaluating the therapeutic benefit of bacterial lysates in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Evaluating the therapeutic benefit of bacterial lysates in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) with exacerbations often triggered by infections. Bacterial lysates have been investigated as interventions to reduce the exacerbations of COPD.

Methods

We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating bacterial lysates (BLs) in adults with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). PubMed, EMBASE, CENTRAL, Web of Science, Google Scholar, ICTRP, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched. In adults with COPD that compared bacterial lysates with placebo or conventional COPD therapy. Primary outcomes were the effect of BLs on exacerbations and duration. Secondary outcomes were hospitalisation risk, the mean number of exacerbations per participant during trial follow up, symptom scores for dyspnoea, sputum, cough, and adverse events. We used random-effects meta-analysis, assessed risk of bias with Cochrane RoB 2, graded certainty with GRADE.

Results

Fifteen RCTs were included. The pooled risk ratio (RR) for exacerbation in patients with COPD treated with BLs vs. control was 0.83 (95% CI 0.74-0.93; P = 0.0009). The mean difference (MD) for exacerbation duration showed no statistical significant reduction -9.26 Days (95% CI -19.56 to 1.03; P = 0.08). Mean number of exacerbations (MD) -0.19 (95% CI -0.30 to -0.08; P = 0.0009). Hospitalisation RR was 0.52 (95% CI 0.35-0.78; P = 0.001).Symptom outcomes were dyspnoea standardised mean difference (SMD) -0.42 (95% CI -0.75 to -0.10; P = 0.01), cough (SMD) -0.37 (95% CI -0.63 to -0.11; P = 0.006), while sputum production showed no significant change (SMD) -0.20 (95% CI -0.65 to 0.25; P = 0.39), The RR for adverse events was 0.95 (95% CI 0.86-1.04; P = 0.27).

Conclusion

Bacterial lysates may be associated with lower COPD exacerbation and hospitalisation risk, with small numerical improvements in dyspnoea, cough, sputum production showed no significant improvement; effects varied by formulation, these findings require confirmation in formulation specific trials.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42024570783, PROSPERO CRD42024570783.

records.title: Association between serum vitamin D levels and the risk of diabetic retinopathy: a meta-analysis.

content.title: Association between serum vitamin D levels and the risk of diabetic retinopathy: a meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Aim

This meta-analysis was conducted to quantitatively synthesize existing evidence on the relationship between serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] levels and diabetic retinopathy (DR).

Methods

A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, the Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library was performed for obtaining observational studies published between January 2015 and February 2026. The included studies reported adjusted effect estimates for the association between 25(OH)D levels and DR. A random-effects model was used to calculate pooled odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Subgroup analysis was performed to explore the sources of heterogeneity based on ethnicity, diabetes type, study design, and vitamin D assay method. A sensitivity analysis was conducted to evaluate the robustness of the pooled results. Publication bias was assessed using Begg's funnel plot and Egger's linear regression test.

Results

This meta-analysis included 16 relevant studies, and the pooled results showed that low serum vitamin D levels were associated with a higher likelihood of developing DR (OR = 1.87, 95% CI: 1.66-2.11). Subgroup analyses revealed stronger effect sizes in Asian populations (OR = 1.97, 95% CI: 1.63-2.38) and type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) patients (OR = 2.15, 95% CI: 1.70-2.72). The sensitivity analysis confirmed the robustness of the findings, and publication bias was not observed.

Conclusion

Low vitamin D levels were associated with higher odds of developing DR, and this association was particularly evident in Asian individuals and T1DM patients. These findings suggest the importance of monitoring vitamin D levels in the management of DR.

records.title: Impact of artificial intelligence on the availability, accessibility, acceptability and quality of ophthalmic disease screening services: a scoping review.

content.title: Impact of artificial intelligence on the availability, accessibility, acceptability and quality of ophthalmic disease screening services: a scoping review.
content.abstract: This scoping review examines the existing literature on the application of artificial intelligence (AI) in screening for eye diseases, with a focus on evaluating whether AI-assisted diagnostic technologies enhance the availability, accessibility, acceptability and quality of screening services. 42 original studies were selected for in-depth analysis, including those employing health economic evaluations. Methodological quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool, with the majority of studies demonstrating high quality-24 scored 5/5, 15 scored 4/5 and the rest scored 3/5. Among the included studies, 34 compared manual screening with either AI-assisted or fully AI-driven approaches. Availability was the most frequently studied aspect (28 studies), followed by acceptability (12 studies), whereas accessibility and service quality were less commonly addressed. Overall, AI shows significant potential to improve the cost-effectiveness of eye care services and enhance patient access, particularly in remote or underserved regions. It was also well-accepted by patients, with high satisfaction and improved referral compliance. The findings suggest that AI holds promise for advancing eye disease screening, although large-scale, long-term trials are needed to effectively integrate AI into the reconstruction of screening processes and the reshaping of eye health service systems.

records.title: A framework of biomarkers for skin aging: a consensus statement by the Aging Biomarker Consortium.

content.title: A framework of biomarkers for skin aging: a consensus statement by the Aging Biomarker Consortium.
content.abstract: Skin is the largest organ of the human body and the first line of defense against the external environment. With the rapid growth of the older population in China, significant challenges have emerged in the prevention and management of age-associated diseases, while skin aging is closely associated with the aging of multiple organs. To address these challenges, the Aging Biomarker Consortium (ABC) has established an expert consensus on biomarkers of skin aging through a review of the literature and consultation with scientists and clinicians. This consensus provides a comprehensive evaluation of the key changes, characteristics, and biomarkers related to skin aging and proposes a systematic framework that categorizes these biomarkers into structural, functional, and humoral biomarkers. Within each dimension, the ABC recommends biomarkers supported by varying levels of clinical and experimental evidence for assessing both physiological and pathological changes in skin tissue during aging, aiming to establish a foundation for the prediction, diagnosis, early detection, and treatment of skin aging and related diseases, with the ultimate goal of improving skin tissue health and promoting healthy aging in elderly populations both in China and worldwide.

records.title: The application of artificial intelligence in myopia prediction for children and adolescents: a review.
records.publisher: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie

content.title: The application of artificial intelligence in myopia prediction for children and adolescents: a review.
content.abstract: Myopia stands as a major threat to the eye health of children and adolescents, impacting their daily lives and academic performance. Early detection and implementation of targeted interventions are critical strategies to prevent myopia onset and slow its progression. Early detection and intervention help prevent and control myopia. With the development of artificial intelligence (AI), AI techniques have gradually been applied in the field of myopia prediction among children and adolescents. This article reviews the application of AI methods in myopia prediction, summarizing key areas such as refractive power prediction, myopia screening, analysis of risk factors, myopia control, pathological myopia analysis and prediction of ocular biological parameters. Furthermore, we highlight the major advancements and challenges in the field of myopia prediction for children and adolescents.

records.title: Explainable Machine Learning Predictive Models for Surgical Site Infections: Scoping Review.

content.title: Explainable Machine Learning Predictive Models for Surgical Site Infections: Scoping Review.
content.abstract:
Background

Surgical site infections (SSIs) remain a major cause of health care-associated infections, and early prediction is essential for improving patient outcomes. Machine learning (ML) has shown potential for SSI prediction; however, clinical implementation requires models that are both accurate and explainable. Despite recent progress in explainable ML, its clinical application to SSI prediction remains limited.

Objective

This study aimed to map explainable ML models for SSI prediction from a clinical perspective and examine their use of structured and unstructured data across the dimensions of data, methodology, and explanation output.

Methods

We conducted a scoping review following PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews) and Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) guidance, and registered the protocol in PROSPERO. Six databases were searched for eligible studies published from January 2010 onward, without language restrictions. The search was conducted on August 9, 2025, and updated on July 14, 2026. We included studies that developed or validated an explainable ML model for predicting SSI in adults. Two reviewers (RS and YL) independently screened studies and extracted data. Findings were narratively synthesized and presented in evidence maps. Methodological quality was assessed using the PROBAST+AI (Prediction model Risk Of Bias Assessment Tool for prediction models using regression or artificial intelligence) methods.

Results

Overall, 77 studies reporting 98 ML models were included. Most models were prognostic (72/98, 73.5%), whereas 26 focused on postoperative SSI diagnosis. A total of 81.8% (63/77) of studies addressed a single surgical specialty, most commonly gastrointestinal surgery (27/63, 42.9%). Overall, 51.9% (40/77) of studies addressed composite SSI predictions. Among all models, % (40/98) were black-box models explained by post hoc methods; SHAP combined with ensemble learning was the leading approach (18/40, 45%). Regression models accounted for half of the inherently interpretable models, interpreted using coefficients. Prognostic models commonly included health and lifestyle (60/72, 83.3%), individual characteristics, and surgical process details (both 57/72, 79.2%); health and lifestyle factors were most frequently important across SSI types. Diagnostic models commonly included surgical process details (13/26, 50%), administrative codes, and individual characteristics (both 10/26, 38.5%). Key diagnostic predictors varied by SSI types: postoperative clinical interventions predominated for composite SSI; vital signs, postoperative interventions, and administrative codes for superficial SSI; postoperative recovery status for deep SSI; and vital signs for organ-space SSI.

Conclusions

Extending previous reviews focusing on model performance, this review mapped explainability methods and important features in SSI prediction, identifying recurring predictor patterns and substantial methodological heterogeneity across prognostic and diagnostic settings. Incomplete reporting of feature definitions and explanatory rationale, together with limited clinical relevance, constrained clinical interpretation and actionability. Clinician-informed reporting frameworks and validation of explanation fidelity and clinical relevance are needed to improve the trustworthiness and utility of SSI prediction models.

records.title: Smoking, alcohol consumption, and psoriasis risk: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of observational studies.

content.title: Smoking, alcohol consumption, and psoriasis risk: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of observational studies.
content.abstract:
Background

Smoking and alcohol consumption are modifiable behavioral exposures of public health relevance that may contribute to psoriasis risk, but the epidemiologic evidence remains inconsistent.

Methods

We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library from inception to December 18, 2025, and included observational studies reporting adjusted associations between smoking or alcohol consumption and the risk of psoriasis. Random-effects meta-analyses and restricted cubic spline models were used where appropriate.

Results

Thirty observational studies involving more than 25 million participants were included. Smoking was associated with a higher risk of psoriasis, with a summary relative estimate of 1.67 (95% CI: 1.46-1.90), and showed evidence of a positive dose-response relationship. Former smokers also remained at higher risk than never smokers (summary relative estimate = 1.38, 95% CI: 1.18-1.62). Alcohol consumption was associated with a smaller increase in psoriasis risk (summary relative estimate = 1.33, 95% CI: 1.16-1.53), and the estimate was further attenuated after trim-and-fill adjustment (summary relative estimate = 1.19, 95% CI: 1.02-1.37), indicating that the alcohol evidence is less robust and should be interpreted cautiously.

Conclusions

Smoking shows a stronger and more consistent association with psoriasis risk, supported by dose-response evidence, whereas alcohol consumption shows a smaller and less consistent association. These findings highlight the public health relevance of smoking cessation and, with caution, alcohol reduction for psoriasis prevention, while also emphasizing the differences in evidence certainty between the two exposures.

Systematic review registration

https://doi.org/10.37766/inplasy2026.1.0086, identifier: INPLASY202610086.

records.title: Operationalising digital and AI pathology in translational research and drug development: an infrastructure and regulatory perspective from biobank to companion diagnostic.

content.title: Operationalising digital and AI pathology in translational research and drug development: an infrastructure and regulatory perspective from biobank to companion diagnostic.
content.abstract: Digital and artificial intelligence (AI) pathology have advanced rapidly and are increasingly embedded in translational research, clinical trials and regulated diagnostic devices. Multiple reviews have addressed the underlying computational methods, oncology applications and clinical translation barriers; however, the operational and regulatory infrastructure required to deploy these technologies across the full drug-development pipeline remains under-reviewed. This structured narrative review synthesises peer-reviewed literature and regulatory documents identified through searches of PubMed, Embase and Web of Science between January 2019 and April 2026 (78 sources retained) on the end-to-end ecosystem connecting AI-ready tissue biobanks, preclinical pathology, AI-assisted patient screening, clinical-trial endpoint adjudication, central pathology review, Contract Research Organization (CRO) workflows and US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulatory pathways governing In Vitro Diagnostics (IVD), Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) and Companion Diagnostics (CDx). Unlike prior method-centric or oncology-clinician-centric reviews, we focus on the infrastructure between models and patients, including Laboratory Information Systems (LIS), Image Management Systems (IMS), AI orchestration and structured reporting under Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments, College of American Pathologists, Good Laboratory Practice, Good Clinical Laboratory Practice, Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act and FDA frameworks. We provide a vendor-agnostic comparison of integrated pathology platforms, a mapping of FDA regulatory pathways (510(k), De Novo, premarket approval) to digital-pathology product categories, a stage-by-stage map from each drug-development challenge to its enabling infrastructure and regulatory framework, and a critical appraisal of the unresolved bottlenecks that gate broad adoption: domain shift, interpretability, annotation cost, algorithmic bias, external validation, regulatory uncertainty and reimbursement. A governed, interoperable LIS, IMS and AI ecosystem is a prerequisite for translating digital-pathology research into regulator-grade evidence. Priorities include external validation against reporting standards (Transparent Reporting of a multivariable prediction model for Individual Prognosis or Diagnosis - Artificial Intelligence (TRIPOD-AI), Checklist for Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging (CLAIM), Development and Early-stage Clinical Identification and Delegation Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence (DECIDE-AI)), harmonisation with the EU AI Act and EU Medical Device Regulation and cost-effectiveness evaluation in real-world deployment.

records.title: Legal and Regulatory Considerations for Artificial Intelligence Use in Medical and Radiology Research.
records.publisher: The Indian journal of radiology & imaging

content.title: Legal and Regulatory Considerations for Artificial Intelligence Use in Medical and Radiology Research.
content.abstract:
Background

Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into medical imaging and radiology research, improving image acquisition, interpretation, workflow efficiency, and decision support. However, its rapid adoption has introduced complex legal and regulatory challenges involving patient privacy, data governance, algorithm validation, liability, intellectual property, transparency, cybersecurity, and ethical oversight. A comprehensive understanding of the evolving legal landscape is essential for the safe, effective, and legally compliant implementation of AI in radiology.

Methods

A narrative review of the published literature and current regulatory guidance was conducted. Relevant international legal and regulatory frameworks governing AI in medical imaging were evaluated, including the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act, General Data Protection Regulation, U.S. Food and Drug Administration guidance on Software as a Medical Device (SaMD), Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, World Health Organization recommendations, International Medical Device Regulators Forum principles, and selected national regulations. Key topics reviewed included data protection, informed consent, AI validation, regulatory approval pathways, post-market surveillance, cybersecurity, algorithmic bias, explainability, and medico-legal responsibility.

Results

Current regulatory frameworks increasingly classify AI-enabled radiology software as SaMD, requiring risk-based evaluation, clinical validation, quality management systems, and continuous post-market performance monitoring. Regulatory authorities emphasize transparency, human oversight, data security, and lifecycle governance of AI systems. Nevertheless, important legal challenges remain, including liability for AI-assisted diagnostic errors, ownership of AI-generated outputs, secondary use of imaging data, cross-border data sharing, algorithmic bias, and regulation of adaptive or continuously learning AI models.

Conclusions

The legal framework governing AI in radiology is evolving in parallel with technological innovation. Responsible integration of AI into clinical practice and research requires harmonized international regulations, robust data governance, standardized validation protocols, transparent algorithm development, and clearly defined legal accountability. Continued collaboration among radiologists, researchers, regulators, policymakers, industry, and legal experts will be essential to ensure that AI technologies remain safe, ethical, equitable, and trustworthy while maximizing their potential to improve patient care.

records.title: A Case-Based Framework for Teaching Artificial Intelligence Applications in Medical Education.
records.publisher: MedEdPORTAL : the journal of teaching and learning resources

content.title: A Case-Based Framework for Teaching Artificial Intelligence Applications in Medical Education.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML)-based tools are emerging across many areas of medicine. The next generation of medical professionals must be prepared to critically assess the tools they will use, including how they work and the ethical or legal implications of their implementation. To address this need, we developed a generalizable case-writing framework that enables educators and learners to engage with clinical cases integrating AI/ML concepts, clinical reasoning, and ethical considerations.

Methods

We designed a case-writing template to compose clinical case scenarios that integrate clinical, technical, and ethical/legal learning objectives relating to AI applications in medicine. Medical students used this template to construct 3 cases. Student-authored cases were presented to a broader audience in 1-hour sessions: first as a pilot event, then as a class-wide lecture for 140 fourth-year medical students in a transition-into-residency course.

Results

After the sessions, student audiences had a statistically significant increase in familiarity with key AI terminology, a greater appreciation for the importance of ethical considerations of AI applications in health care, and an increased perceived importance of integrating AI-related topics into the medical curriculum.

Discussion

A case-based framework provides a scalable approach to integrating AI education into existing curricula by connecting clinical scenarios with technical concepts and the ethical considerations of AI adoption; cases offer a familiar format that helps learners understand AI applications in patient care while exploring implementation challenges. The case-writing template and 3 sample cases are provided as adaptable resources for educators seeking to incorporate AI literacy.

records.title: Integrating predictive modeling, imaging, and EHR-linked decision support in spine informatics.
records.publisher: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society

content.title: Integrating predictive modeling, imaging, and EHR-linked decision support in spine informatics.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming spine care by enabling analysis of imaging, clinical, and textual data to support diagnosis, risk stratification, and treatment planning. Techniques including deep learning-based image analysis, radiomics, and natural language processing (NLP) offer opportunities to standardize interpretation and derive quantitative biomarkers beyond human visual assessment. This narrative review examines recent innovations in spine-focused biomedical informatics and evaluates their clinical relevance and translational challenges.

Methods

A narrative review was conducted, focusing on AI in spine care across imaging, radiomics, NLP of electronic health records, and clinical decision support. Literature was selected via targeted PubMed searches; studies describing technical development, validation, and clinical implementation were synthesized, addressing explainability, uncertainty, workflow, and regulation.

Results

Convolutional neural networks enable vertebral and disc segmentation, detection of degenerative and traumatic pathology, and quantitative assessment of paraspinal musculature. Radiomics approaches extract high-dimensional imaging features that improve the prediction of osteoporosis, fracture risk, tumor characterization, and surgical outcomes. NLP techniques, including emerging large language models, unlock clinically relevant information from unstructured text, enhancing outcome prediction and population-level analyses. Multimodal clinical decision support systems integrating imaging, EHR data, and NLP-derived features demonstrate promise for personalized risk assessment and treatment guidance. Challenges remain regarding data heterogeneity, generalizability, privacy, and prospective validation.

Conclusion

AI-driven biomedical informatics holds substantial promise to enhance diagnostic accuracy, prognostication, and personalized decision-making in spine care. Successful clinical translation will require robust validation, explainable, uncertainty-aware models, regulatory alignment, and integration into clinical workflows to ensure safe, trustworthy, and patient-centered adoption.

records.title: Toward explainable traffic crash liability analysis via neural-symbolic multimodal reasoning: Integrating visual perception with legal knowledge graphs.

content.title: Toward explainable traffic crash liability analysis via neural-symbolic multimodal reasoning: Integrating visual perception with legal knowledge graphs.
content.abstract: Determining traffic crash liability relies on rigorous on-site evidence and legal provisions and involves substantial manual intervention and potential human error. However, intelligent traffic monitoring systems focus on detection and tracking and cannot provide structured, rule-grounded decision support for formal crash-liability analysis. Moreover, emerging multimodal large language models (MLLMs) suffer from object hallucination that distorts or omits physical evidence, and their opaque reasoning cannot produce explicit evidence-to-rule chains required for traceable and reviewable liability analysis. This paper proposes CrashLex, an explainable neural-symbolic decision-support framework that integrates visual perception with legal knowledge graph reasoning to align multimodal inference with predefined statutory rules and traceability requirements. Within CrashLex, a dual-query vision-language architecture employs parallel semantic and symbolic streams to mitigate object hallucination, utilizing Scene Queries for global context modeling and Perception Queries for fine-grained atomic feature extraction, respectively. The domain-specific legal knowledge graph maps these atomic facts from observable physical conditions to corresponding statutory elements, providing a structured basis for rule-grounded assessment. A logic-driven aggregation protocol then imposes explicit constraints derived from extracted facts and statutory provisions onto the inference process, thereby enabling traceable and interpretable preliminary liability assessment. On the held-out DeepAccident benchmark, CrashLex achieves a Legal Accuracy of 94.0% under the fixed legal-output evaluation protocol and an Object Hallucination Rate of 2.8%, corresponding to an 82.1% relative reduction from the 15.6% rate of the best-performing MLLM baseline on this metric. CrashLex grounds its assessment results in the deterministic execution of predefined legal rules rather than relying solely on unconstrained probabilistic generation, providing verifiable reasoning chains for rule-grounded human review.

records.title: Beyond Accuracy: Validation, Reproducibility, and Deployment Readiness of AI in Food Safety and Quality.

content.title: Beyond Accuracy: Validation, Reproducibility, and Deployment Readiness of AI in Food Safety and Quality.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly proposed for detecting microbial and chemical hazards in food, but laboratory accuracies are rarely reproduced in routine use. This structured narrative review examined whether reported performance is traceable, independently validated, and transferable to operational settings. Eight bibliographic databases and seven institutional routes were searched for English-language records published from January 2018 to May 2026, and we screened the records; the final corpus comprised 76 sources (53 journal articles, 9 conference papers, 2 preprints, and 12 institutional or regulatory documents). Seven primary studies supporting the quantitative evidence were appraised individually against 11 indicators, including test-set independence, external validation, and leakage control. Physical-hazard inspection and narrow-matrix spectral grading had the strongest deployment evidence, whereas microbial and chemical screening remained at laboratory or pilot scale. Among the appraised studies, the most credible estimates came from physically or temporally independent test sets, and no sensor-based study evaluated transfer to another instrument or laboratory. Deep learning showed clear advantages for image-based tasks but not consistently for small-sample spectral calibration. Adoption is limited mainly by validation design, recalibration burden, false-alarm costs, and the absence of a regulatory pathway rather than by accuracy. AI is best positioned as a screening and decision-support layer linked to confirmatory testing and human oversight.

records.title: Assessment, intervention, and ethical considerations of artificial intelligence for depression and suicide risk: A scoping review.

content.title: Assessment, intervention, and ethical considerations of artificial intelligence for depression and suicide risk: A scoping review.
content.abstract:
Background

Depression and suicidal behavior constitute leading causes of global disease burden. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers promise for improving detection, intervention, and prevention, yet no comprehensive review has simultaneously mapped AI-driven assessment, intervention, and ethical considerations across both conditions.

Objective

To systematically map AI applications for depression and suicide risk across three thematic axes: (1) assessment and diagnosis, (2) conversational AI and AI-driven interventions, and (3) ethical, equity, and regulatory considerations, and to evaluate translational maturity using a novel framework.

Methods

Following JBI scoping review methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidelines, six databases were searched from January 2020 through March 2026. Two independent reviewers screened 5079 records using a two-stage process, yielding 2844 included studies (Cohen's kappa = 0.66). Data were extracted using a standardized charting form with AI-assisted full-text analysis.

Results

Assessment/diagnosis dominated (n = 1785), with fewer intervention studies (n = 318). Large language model-related studies rose from <1% (2020-2022) to 11.1% (2025) of included studies annually. Translational Readiness Framework classification revealed 44.8% Laboratory, 49.2% Bridge, and 6.0% Clinical stage, with intervention studies showing the highest Clinical-stage proportion (16.7% vs. 5.9% for assessment). Five cross-cutting observations emerged, including an inverted evidence pyramid and persistent cross-axis integration gap (4.4%).

Conclusion

Despite technical advances, the evidence base remains concentrated at early translational stages. The proposed Translational Readiness Framework provides a structured lens for evaluating progress and guiding research prioritization. Closing the gap between laboratory promise and clinical impact requires a shift from model-centric to patient-centric research and from benchmark performance to real-world validation.

records.title: AI-Enabled Animal Behavior Analysis for Translational Pharmacology and Therapeutic Discovery.

content.title: AI-Enabled Animal Behavior Analysis for Translational Pharmacology and Therapeutic Discovery.
content.abstract: Animal behavior is a critical endpoint in preclinical pharmacology, toxicology, and therapeutic discovery, yet conventional behavioral scoring remains labor-intensive, low-dimensional, and difficult to reproduce across laboratories. Artificial intelligence (AI) can now quantify behavior from video with greater spatial, temporal, and phenotypic resolution. This review summarizes how object detection, markerless pose estimation, unsupervised behavioral segmentation, foundation models, and autonomous analysis agents are reshaping behavioral phenotyping. General-purpose object detectors rapidly localize and track animals, whereas open-source pose-estimation tools extend measurement beyond centroid tracking to body-part trajectories and fine motor patterns; paired with supervised classifiers, they have matched human scoring and exceeded some commercial systems. Technical accuracy alone does not establish behavioral construct validity or pharmacological validity. Unsupervised methods such as Motion Sequencing represent drug responses and disease-model phenotypes as structured changes in behavioral states rather than only as predefined endpoints, providing high-dimensional fingerprints of pharmacological action. Segmentation and tracking foundation models may reduce annotation burden but require validation across species, strain, sex, apparatus, and paradigm. AI agents may assist with literature review, code generation, analysis auditing, and figure production but must remain within transparent, human-supervised workflows. In behavioral pharmacology, pose estimation is established as a measurement method and emerging as a drug-effect endpoint, supervised classification and unsupervised segmentation are emerging, and foundation models and agents remain prospective. AI-enabled behavioral analysis can become a reproducible phenotyping layer for drug discovery and toxicology if researchers adopt open pipelines, rigorous validation, and reporting standards, rather than replacing one opaque measurement system with another.

records.title: Artificial intelligence-based voice biomarkers for early detection and monitoring of neurological diseases: current evidence, limitations, and clinical perspectives.

content.title: Artificial intelligence-based voice biomarkers for early detection and monitoring of neurological diseases: current evidence, limitations, and clinical perspectives.
content.abstract:
Background

Early diagnosis and longitudinal monitoring of neurological diseases remain major clinical challenges because current diagnostic approaches are often expensive, invasive, or insufficiently sensitive to detect early functional changes. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising approach for analyzing voice and speech as non-invasive digital biomarkers capable of capturing subtle alterations associated with neurological dysfunction.

Methods

This narrative review analyzed studies published between 2015 and 2026 retrieved from PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar. The review critically examines the limitations of current neurological diagnostic methods, summarizes the available evidence on AI-based voice and speech biomarkers, discusses machine learning and deep learning approaches applied to speech analysis, and evaluates the methodological, ethical, and regulatory challenges that currently limit their clinical implementation.

Results

Current evidence indicates that AI-based voice biomarkers have considerable potential for screening, diagnostic support, and longitudinal monitoring of neurological disorders, including Parkinson's disease, Alzheimer's disease, multiple sclerosis, and other neurodegenerative conditions. Several studies report high diagnostic performance under controlled experimental settings. However, substantial heterogeneity in study design, sample size, languages, speech acquisition protocols, validation strategies, and reporting standards limits direct comparison between studies and hinders clinical translation. External validation and prospective multicenter studies remain scarce.

Conclusion

AI-based voice analysis represents a promising, scalable, and non-invasive complement to conventional neurological assessment, with particular potential for remote screening and disease monitoring. Nevertheless, current evidence does not yet support routine clinical implementation. Future progress will depend on standardized speech acquisition protocols, robust external validation across diverse populations, explainable AI models, and regulatory frameworks capable of ensuring safety, reproducibility, and clinical reliability.

records.title: Explainable fMRI decoding reveals neurobiological signatures of emotional arousal complementary to traditional analyses.

content.title: Explainable fMRI decoding reveals neurobiological signatures of emotional arousal complementary to traditional analyses.
content.abstract: Objective.Understanding how emotional arousal is represented in the brain is fundamental for elucidating affective regulation and its alterations in autism spectrum disorder. Classical neuroimaging approaches, such as the general linear model (GLM), have provided important insights into emotional processing. However, the extent to which data-driven decoding and traditional model-based analyses provide complementary information about emotional arousal remains unclear.Approach.We introduce an explainable artificial intelligence framework that combines the lightweight functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) decoder (fMRINet) with Deep Learning Important FeaTures to derive data-driven neurobiological signatures of emotional arousal. The framework enables interpretation of spatiotemporal neural contributions during emotional processing. We applied the framework to fMRI data acquired while neurotypically and autistic participants viewed naturalistic emotional videos and compared the resulting signatures with categorical and parametric GLM analyses.Main results.The framework identified distinct spatiotemporal neurobiological signatures associated with emotional arousal. Neurotypical participants engaged a distributed perceptual-limbic-prefrontal network under high arousal and frontoparietal executive regions under low arousal. In contrast, autistic participants exhibited a more spatially restricted and posterior-biased pattern under high arousal, with reduced ventromedial prefrontal and limbic contributions, while low-arousal patterns resembled typically developing, suggesting preserved executive mechanisms during low-arousal processing. The GLM analyses revealed partly convergent and partly distinct findings: categorical GLM detected no significant group differences, whereas parametric GLM identified widespread cortical-subcortical modulation in neurotypical individuals and cerebellar-restricted effects in autistic, consistent with compensatory reliance on motor-timing circuits.Significance. The proposed framework provides an interpretable, data-driven perspective on emotional processing and reveals neurobiologically plausible patterns consistent with existing literature. Together, the explainable decoding and GLM results highlight complementary aspects of emotional arousal processing, suggesting that explainable decoding approaches may provide additional insights alongside traditional model-based neuroimaging analyses.

records.title: Augmentation or erosion? Artificial intelligence and the transformation of clinical reasoning: a critical narrative review.

content.title: Augmentation or erosion? Artificial intelligence and the transformation of clinical reasoning: a critical narrative review.
content.abstract:
Background

Artificial intelligence (AI) systems are used to support diagnosis, but a model's accuracy does not establish that clinicians reason more accurately when they use it. This review appraises how AI decision support and large language models affect physicians' diagnostic performance and the risks of relying on them.

Methods

This critical narrative review follows the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles. Scopus, PubMed/MEDLINE, SciELO and LILACS were searched in July and August 2026 in English, Spanish and Portuguese. Eligible studies, published from 2015 onward, compared AI-assisted with unassisted clinicians, measured reliance on AI or unassisted performance after exposure to it, or externally validated deployed models. A single author selected sources purposively. Nine primary studies were appraised with an adapted Critical Appraisal Skills Programme framework.

Results

In randomized trials of perceptual tasks, AI support improved detection. In the MASAI mammography screening trial, cancer detection rose from 5.0 to 6.4 per 1,000 women, reading workload fell by 44%, and the interval-cancer rate was non-inferior. In colonoscopy, computer-aided detection raised the adenoma detection rate from 40.4% to 54.8%. In the only randomized trial of open-ended diagnostic reasoning, access to GPT-4 did not improve physicians' scores (76% vs. 74%; P=.60 ), although the model alone scored 92%. Evidence of harm came from smaller or non-randomized studies: reader accuracy fell sharply when AI suggestions were incorrect or the AI missed a cancer; physicians trained in AI literacy were still misled by erroneous model advice; unassisted adenoma detection fell from 28.4% to 22.4% after routine AI use in one pre-post study; and a deployed sepsis model discriminated poorly on external validation (area under the curve 0.63). No eligible study from Latin America was identified.

Conclusions

In the studies reviewed, AI assistance improved clinician performance in bounded detection tasks but not in open-ended diagnostic reasoning, where evidence is limited to one vignette-based trial. The evidence that reliance on AI can impair performance comes from single or design-limited studies and does not establish how large or lasting such effects are. Benefit therefore cannot be inferred from model accuracy alone; assisted and unassisted clinician performance should be measured directly.

records.title: Digital health and artificial intelligence in paediatric respiratory medicine: what clinicians need to know and what is coming next.

content.title: Digital health and artificial intelligence in paediatric respiratory medicine: what clinicians need to know and what is coming next.
content.abstract: Digital health and artificial intelligence (AI) are increasingly part of paediatric respiratory clinics, from home-based symptom monitoring and remote consultations to AI-supported test interpretation and large language model (LLM)-supported communication. These tools promise to capture real-world disease and treatment patterns, support self-management, and enhance clinical decisions. Yet for most of these tools, the paediatric evidence base remains limited and fragmented, and the clinical benefit observed in practice is often modest. What has emerged is that effectiveness depends less on the technology itself than on how it fits into the child-parent-clinician triad, on its usability in daily family life, and on its impact on clinical workflow and on equity. Paediatric datasets remain small, heterogeneous and developmental, making extrapolation from adult evidence risky. Over the next 3 years, progress is likely to consolidate rather than expand, with paediatric-specific validation, regulation and routine integration. Clinicians will play a central role: deciding what to adopt, what to question, and what to govern.

records.title: Clinical integration of artificial intelligence for diagnosis, risk prediction and management of rare cardiovascular diseases.
records.publisher: Journal of basic and clinical physiology and pharmacology

content.title: Clinical integration of artificial intelligence for diagnosis, risk prediction and management of rare cardiovascular diseases.
content.abstract:
Introduction

RCDs comprise a diverse group of inherited and acquired disorders characterized by low prevalence, substantial genetic and phenotypic heterogeneity, delayed diagnosis, and limited evidence-based therapeutic options. These challenges contribute to poor clinical outcomes, including progressive heart failure, malignant arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death.

Content

This review summarizes recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) for the diagnosis and management of RCDs. AI technologies, including machine learning, deep learning, and multimodal data integration, enable comprehensive analysis of electrocardiography, echocardiography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, computed tomography, genomic and multi-omics data, biomarkers, wearable devices, and electronic health records. These approaches improve early disease detection, phenotypic classification, risk stratification, prognostic prediction and personalized treatment planning.

Summary

Current evidence suggests that AI significantly enhances diagnostic accuracy, prognostic assessment, and individualized clinical decision-making in patients with RCDs.

Outlook

Future clinical implementation requires standardized multicenter datasets, prospective validation, transparent and explainable algorithms, robust regulatory and ethical frameworks, and seamless integration into healthcare systems. Continued interdisciplinary collaboration will accelerate AI-driven precision cardiovascular medicine and improve outcomes for patients with rare cardiovascular diseases.

records.title: Mitigating Domain Shift and Dataset Bias in Deep Learning Models for Cancer Diagnostics.
records.publisher: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine

content.title: Mitigating Domain Shift and Dataset Bias in Deep Learning Models for Cancer Diagnostics.
content.abstract: The translation of deep learning architectures from controlled experimental settings into real-world cancer diagnostics is heavily bottlenecked by domain shift and demographic bias. While models routinely achieve near-perfect retrospective performance on internal datasets, validation across external multicenter cohorts incurs a systemic and severe performance degradation, with an average metric drop of 0.16 AUC. This review provides a comprehensive metasynthesis of contemporary algorithmic mitigation paradigms designed to alleviate distribution discrepancies, evaluating techniques ranging from classical stain normalization and adversarial feature alignment to test-time adaptation and large-scale self-supervised pathology foundation models. Our analysis reveals a critical dichotomy between raw diagnostic performance and algorithmic equity: current optimization frameworks that successfully elevate aggregate macro metrics frequently do so by obscuring or actively exacerbating underlying demographic and subpopulation disparities. To achieve safe, equitable, and universally reliable clinical artificial intelligence, the field must transcend static validation habits. We outline a future roadmap anchored on three critical axes: establishing intersectional disparity indices as primary regulatory endpoints, standardizing multivendor metadata-rich benchmarks, and prioritizing.

records.title: Growth, Specialty Distribution, and Regulatory Pathways of Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Medical Devices Authorized in the United States From 1995 to 2026: A Cross-Sectional Analysis.

content.title: Growth, Specialty Distribution, and Regulatory Pathways of Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Medical Devices Authorized in the United States From 1995 to 2026: A Cross-Sectional Analysis.
content.abstract: Introduction The United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) publishes a list of artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled medical devices authorized for marketing. Annual authorizations have risen sharply in recent years, and an updated analysis of the complete list is needed. This study aimed to characterize regulatory authorizations on the full list through mid-2026. Methods A cross-sectional analysis of all 1,614 entries on the FDA AI-Enabled Medical Device List (final decisions from September 1995 to June 2026) was performed. Regulatory pathway, year, lead review panel, product code, and manufacturer group were derived for each entry. Growth was estimated by log-linear regression, trends were tested with the Cochran-Armitage test and logistic regression with manufacturer-clustered standard errors, and associations were tested with chi-squared and Fisher exact tests, with Holm adjustment for multiple testing. Results Annual authorizations rose from 18 in 2016 to 335 in 2025, an estimated growth of 35.3% per year (95% confidence interval (CI) 27.0-44.3), and 977 of 1,614 entries (60.5%) were authorized from 2023 onward. Radiology accounted for 1,230 entries (76.2%); its share peaked at 347 of 405 (85.7%) in 2020-2022 and fell to 750 of 977 (76.8%) in 2023-2026 (p < 0.001), while radiology authorizations kept growing in absolute terms and the number of represented specialty panels rose from 10 to 16. The 510(k) pathway accounted for 1,553 authorizations (96.2%), and radiology entries were less likely than others to use the De Novo or premarket approval pathways (18 of 1,230, 1.5% vs. 43 of 384, 11.2%; odds ratio 0.14, 95% CI 0.08-0.27 after adjustment for era). Of 40 De Novo grants, 22 created product codes that later received 181 510(k) clearances. Imaging systems such as ultrasound, computed tomography, and magnetic resonance scanners accounted for 399 entries (24.7%), and seven large manufacturers accounted for 288 of these (72.2%). Findings were similar for 1,195 deduplicated devices and for entries through December 2025. Conclusions FDA authorization of AI-enabled devices continues to accelerate. Radiology remains dominant and still growing, while other specialties are expanding alongside it; the 510(k) pathway predominates, and a growing share of authorizations concerns AI embedded in imaging equipment. These findings describe regulatory authorizations rather than clinical adoption, and they identify transparency about AI functions in conventional devices and AI-specific post-market surveillance as topics for further study.

records.title: 4D nanoimaging-guided smart therapeutics: spatiotemporal control of disease microenvironments.

content.title: 4D nanoimaging-guided smart therapeutics: spatiotemporal control of disease microenvironments.
content.abstract: A revolutionary shift in the field of nanotheranostics is the development of smart therapeutics guided by 4D nanoimaging, which addresses the shortcomings of traditional platforms that rely on static imaging and passive drug delivery. The spatial and temporal control of these systems can be accurately tuned to modulate dynamics in disease microenvironment assays, especially for complex diseases, such as cancer and inflammatory diseases. Recent developments in stimulus-responsive nanomaterials and real-time visualization modalities have enabled more specific and less damaging adaptive, feedback-based therapeutic interventions. This review presents an overview of the recent literature on the design, operating principles, and biomedical applications of 4D nanoimaging-guided smart therapeutics. Particular attention is paid to building nanoplatforms that are responsive to endogenous and exogenous signals and advanced imaging tools (e.g., near-infrared fluorescence and photoacoustic imaging), as well as integrating them with artificial intelligence to establish predictive and closed-loop therapeutic platforms. Applicable literature has been critically reviewed with regards to the performance parameters of spatial-temporal resolution, therapy release performance, and therapeutic effects. The reviewed literature shows how the 4D nanoimaging platforms reach high spatiotemporal precision to allow real-time monitoring of the biodistribution of nanoparticles and disease progression. The controlled drug release efficiencies of the stimuli-responsive systems typically range from 70% to 90%, and the integration of multimodal imaging provides better diagnostic performance and tissue penetration.
